newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican, Venezuelan presidents discuss Ecuador crisis.
newsitem.headline: Mexican, Venezuelan presidents discuss Ecuador crisis.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo and Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera discussed the crisis in Ecuador on Thursday and expressed concern about the situation there, a senior Mexican Foreign Ministry source said.
"It's a delicate matter. Regionally, it is indeed delicate," the source said.
It was not known whether Zedillo and Caldera, who is on a state visit to Mexico, would make a joint statement on the Ecuadoran crisis.

Ecuador's President Abdala Bucaram faces a possible congressional attempt to force him out of office, and trade unions have launched a general strike in protest against price rises resulting from his austerity policies.
Zedillo and Caldera also discussed their Group of Three trade agreement, which also includes Colombia, and other bilateral issues.

After his meeting with Zedillo, Caldera tripped on a carpet and fell at Mexico City's Altar to the Homeland. Witnesses said the 81-year-old Venezuelan leader bloodied his nose but a doctor attended him immediately and he continued his programme without interruption.
"Fortunately he's fine. Nothing happened, thank God," a Venezuelan diplomat said.
Caldera was scheduled to return to Venezuela on Saturday after making a private visit to the shrine of the Virgin of Guadalupe, Mexico's patron saint.
